Egregious

ih-GREE-jus -- stress on the second syllable, GREE. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Egregious is outstandingly bad or shocking.

The newspaper printed an egregious misquote that turned the mayor's promise into its exact opposite.

Worked Example

In the final minute of the championship, a defender catches the ball with both hands inside his own penalty area, two steps from the referee.

That foul is egregious: not a borderline call but a violation so shockingly bad it stands out from every ordinary mistake around it. Egregious attaches to errors, lies, and offenses that leap out for their sheer badness.

How Egregious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

flagrant

flagrant: obviously and boldly offensive

glaring

glaring: painfully obvious, as a fault or error

Antonyms

minor

minor: small and unimportant

trivial

trivial: of little value or consequence

How Strong Is It? — glaring → egregious → flagrant

glaring vs. egregious

glaring vs. egregious: Glaring is a step gentler than egregious -- a glaring mistake is impossible to miss, while an egregious one is so outrageously bad that missing it would be a scandal in itself.

flagrant vs. egregious

flagrant vs. egregious: Flagrant outdoes even egregious in defiance: an egregious violation is shockingly bad, while a flagrant one is committed openly and brazenly, almost daring anyone watching to object.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out of, from (a form of Latin ex-)

Root — greg

Root — greg: flock, herd (Latin grex, gregis 'flock')

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: E- ('out of', a form of ex-) + greg ('flock', Latin grex) + -ious ('full of') spell egregious, using the -ious variant of this unit's suffix family -- literally 'standing out from the flock.' For the Romans egregius was a compliment: outstandingly GOOD. English speakers then used it so sarcastically ('oh, an egregious performance indeed') that the irony stuck, and the word flipped to mean standing out for sheer badness. Today an egregious error is one that leaves the flock of ordinary mistakes far behind.

Use the root in a new word: gregarious

Use the root in a new word: gregarious: The gregarious puppy greeted every stranger at the dog park like a long-lost friend.

Root Check

Word Choice

Egregious wants a noun of wrongdoing after it: an egregious error, an egregious lie, an egregious violation, an egregious foul. It judges deeds rather than souls -- for a deliberately evil person or plot, this unit gives you nefarious instead, and for harm that sneaks in slowly, insidious. Egregious badness is loud, obvious, and out in the open.
